content: GLMN, also known as Glomulin, is a protein in humans that is encoded by the GLMN gene. This gene produces a phosphorylated protein that is a component of a Skp1-Cullin-F-box-like complex. The GLMN protein plays a critical role in the normal development of the vascular system. Mutations in the GLMN gene have been linked to glomuvenous malformations, which are also referred to as glomangiomas. There are alternatively spliced variants of the GLMN gene that encode different protein isoforms. However, the complete structure of only one of these isoforms has been fully characterized to date. In terms of molecular interactions, GLMN has been demonstrated to interact with FKBP52, C-Met, and FKBP1A.
